subsystems.name: Compute engine
subsystems.role: runs the neural network's tensor operations.
parts: GPU or NPU for matrix multiplication

subsystems.name: Memory
subsystems.role: holds model weights and the key-value cache during inference.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: supplies stable voltage and removes heat within a small enclosure.

subsystems.name: Storage and I/O
subsystems.role: loads models quickly and connects to sensors, networks and displays.

subsystems.name: Software stack

buildSteps.title: Define the target
buildSteps.detail: Set the maximum model size (in billions of parameters), token throughput, power budget (often 10–60 W) and required ports.

buildSteps.title: Select or design the SoC
buildSteps.detail: Choose a chip with an NPU or GPU that accelerates matrix math, or design one with enough on-chip memory to avoid bottlenecks.

buildSteps.title: Integrate memory
buildSteps.detail: Solder LPDDR5 packages close to the SoC for high bandwidth, or use on-package high-bandwidth memory where the design allows.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the PCB
buildSteps.detail: Lay out high-speed differential pairs for memory and PCIe, manage power planes and impedance, then manufacture the multi-layer board.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the board
buildSteps.detail: Pick-and-place the SoC, memory, power stages and connectors, reflow-solder them, and underfill the largest chips for reliability.

buildSteps.title: Test and bin
buildSteps.detail: Run functional tests, measure memory bandwidth and thermal performance under sustained load, and sort boards by stable clock speed.

buildSteps.title: Write firmware and drivers
buildSteps.detail: Bring up the bootloader, power management and accelerator drivers so the operating system can use the NPU and memory correctly.

buildSteps.title: Build the software stack
buildSteps.detail: Port an inference runtime, add quantization support (e.g., 4-bit and 8-bit), and provide tools to convert popular model formats.

buildSteps.title: Validate real workloads
buildSteps.detail: Run representative language models, measure tokens per second and power draw, and tune scheduling so the board stays within its thermal limit.

prerequisites.tech: NPUs or GPUs with matrix-multiply acceleration
prerequisites.why: general-purpose CPUs are far too slow for real-time language model inference.
holding billions of parameters needs tens of gigabytes and hundreds of gigabytes per second; LPDDR5 is affordable but HBM remains costly and power-hungry.
reducing weights to 4 or 8 bits shrinks models enough to fit in edge memory with modest quality loss.
they map model graphs onto the available accelerators and manage the key-value cache to avoid recomputation.
sustained inference produces heat that must be removed from a small, often fanless enclosure.

pathway.milestone: developer boards with 8–32 GB of memory run quantized 7–13 billion parameter models at a few tokens per second
pathway.unlocks: local chatbots, document search and private inference without cloud calls.

pathway.milestone: unified memory of 64–128 GB on a single board
pathway.unlocks: running 70 billion parameter models locally for more capable assistants and coding tools.

pathway.milestone: chiplet designs with on-package high-bandwidth memory exceeding 1 TB/s
pathway.unlocks: faster token generation and support for larger context windows.
personalized AI that adapts to a user's data without sending it to a data centre.
